doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: John Bunch, Jay Leonhart and ad executives in the booth
summary: Jay Leonhart calms John Bunch; dealing with agency people.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: John Bunch — he used to get nervous when he was on a jingle. He’d get nervous. And I remember it was me, Jay Leonhart, John Bunch, I forget who else. Small band. And Jay Leonhart did the same thing to John Bunch. He said, “Just play the way you play, man, don’t let them —” you know they were asking him for things to do and he was getting nervous. Because John usually, you know he didn’t do a lot of recording, he just did all
beautiful gigs you know, beautiful recordings with good singers. But Jay Leonhart saved him. I remember Jay, he says, “Hey man, just play, you know, don’t listen to them.”
Did you ever have an ad exec hanging out in the booth trying to tell you like —

Oh yes, oh yes, yes. Yeah that’s quite — it’s very tricky man. It’s like you know I’m going to try to do it, whatever they want, you know and it’s all attitude. It’s like your attitude with the person you know. It’s like I honestly want to please this person. You know what I mean man? You don’t run from it. You kind of like wow, let’s see, I think he likes this, let me try that and that kind of thing. But nobody ever got weird or anything or indignant or anything like that you know. We always, everybody was always nice you know.
